source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, History Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. The Vedas
points: The **Vedas** are among the oldest texts of India, composed in **Sanskrit** and preserved orally for centuries (**shruti** = "that which is heard").

sub: **Rigveda** — the oldest; hymns to deities such as **Agni, Indra, Varuna, Soma, Usha**.

points: The Rigveda names the land of **Sapta-Sindhu** (seven rivers) and praises the river **Sarasvati**.

sections.heading: 2. Key Ideas of Vedic Thought
points: **Rita** — the cosmic order/natural law that keeps the universe in balance.
**Yajna** — ritual sacrifice/offering (often into fire) to maintain harmony.
**Upanishads** — later Vedic texts of philosophy; explore **atman** (the inner self) and **brahman** (the ultimate reality), and teach that the two are ultimately one.
Ideas of **dharma** (right conduct/duty), **karma** (action and its results) and **rebirth** took shape.

sections.heading: 3. Jainism
points: Taught by **Vardhamana Mahavira**, the **24th (and last) tirthankara** ("ford-maker").
**Ahimsa** (non-violence) is the central and most important teaching.
**Five vows:** non-violence, truth, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possession (aparigraha).
**Anekantavada** — the idea that truth has many sides.
Path of **asceticism** and self-discipline to free the soul.

sections.heading: 4. Buddhism
points: Taught by **Gautama Buddha** (Siddhartha), the "Enlightened One," who attained enlightenment at **Bodh Gaya**.
**Four Noble Truths:** there is suffering (dukkha); it has a cause (desire); it can end; the way to end it is the Eightfold Path.
**Eightfold Path** — the **Middle Path** between extreme luxury and extreme penance.
Goal = **nirvana** (end of suffering and the cycle of rebirth).
Taught in the language of ordinary people (Prakrit/Pali).

sections.heading: 5. Many Streams of Culture
points: Indian culture grew from **several streams**, not one: Vedic, Jain, Buddhist, and **tribal/folk** traditions.
**Oral traditions**, songs and stories carried knowledge across generations.
In the south, **Sangam literature** (in **Tamil**) records a rich early culture.
These streams mingled and enriched one another — a rooted yet plural heritage.

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Four Vedas: Rigveda (oldest), Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda; language = Sanskrit; shruti = heard.
Rita = cosmic order; Yajna = sacrifice; Upanishads = atman & brahman.
Mahavira = 24th tirthankara; Jain core = ahimsa; anekantavada = many-sidedness of truth.
Buddha = Four Noble Truths + Eightfold (Middle) Path; goal = nirvana; enlightenment at Bodh Gaya.
Sangam literature = early Tamil (southern) tradition.

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Rigveda is the oldest** Veda — not the Atharvaveda.
Mahavira was the **24th** tirthankara (the last), not the founder from scratch.
The Buddha's path is the **Middle Path** — avoiding both luxury and extreme penance.
Vedas are **shruti** (heard/oral); they were preserved by memory before being written.
